newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Daewoo says still interested in Thomson Multimedia.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo says still interested in Thomson Multimedia.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Corp said on Wednesday it remained interested in bidding for France's Thomson Multimedia (TMM) if invited.

Terence Billing, a spokesman for Daewoo Group, corporate and marketing communications, told a news conference in Rabat: "Daewoo Group remains extremely interested in the French Thomson Multimedia firm."
Billing was speaking after the signing ceremony of a $28 million deal under which Daewoo has bought Morocco's five-star Hyatt Regency hotel, now called the Hilton hotel.
"I would like to insist on the fact that the Daewoo Group is interested in Thomson Multimedia and would re-tender if invited to by the French authorities," Billing said.
He declined to give further details on Daewoo's investment intentions in France in future.

France last year called off a plan to sell the Thomson SA group, which owns defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF and television manufacturer Thomson Multimedia, after its privatisation commission objected.
The government had previously expressed a preference for selling Thomson SA to Lagardere, which had planned to sell on Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo.
The government since decided to sell Thomson-CSF alone, and announced it would do so by private placement.
Daewoo said it plans to invest up to $900 million in Morocco in various sectors including telecommunications.
"It will be the biggest investment of our group in the North Africa region," a Daewoo official said on Wednesday.
